pair.title: Connect a phone
pair.body: An Android phone plugged into a computer by USB is connected by the Jeeta device bridge program on that computer. Pairing gives the program its key.
pair.dialogDescription: Creates a key for one computer, with the one permission a bridge needs (devices.bridge).
pair.nameHint: Name it after the computer, e.g. Workshop PC.
pair.keyDescription: Copy the key now; the three steps to run the bridge are below.
pair.step1: On the computer the phone is plugged into, install adb (Android SDK Platform-Tools). On the phone, turn on Developer options and USB debugging, connect it by USB and allow this computer when the phone asks.
pair.step2: Put the program jeeta-device-bridge.exe in a folder (where to get it: section 4 of docs/operations/device-bridge.md), and beside it a file named jeeta-device-bridge.toml with this content:
pair.keyEnv: You can leave the key out of the file and set it in the JEETA_DEVICE_BRIDGE_KEY environment variable instead.
pair.step3: Run jeeta-device-bridge.exe. Within about 15 seconds each phone it sees appears under Devices on this page, verified. To start it at every logon:
pair.ownKey: Each computer's bridge needs a key of its own: Jeeta tells bridges apart by their keys, and refuses a phone that another running bridge holds. For another computer, pair again.

failure.recipientNotAllowed: the recipient is not on the Meta test number's allowed list. Add the number as a recipient in Meta under WhatsApp → API Setup, or connect a real WhatsApp number.
failure.windowClosed: more than 24 hours have passed since the customer's last message; only an approved template can be sent now.
failure.reconnect: the account's sign-in expired or was refused; reconnect it on the Connect page.
failure.permission: the account lacks the permission for this; grant the requested permissions or reconnect it.
failure.throttled: the provider asked us to slow down; try again a little later.
failure.configuration: the account's sending settings could not be read; check and reconnect it.
failure.xCredits: the X API has no credits; add credits in the X developer console (console.x.com).
failure.xDuplicate: X does not publish the same text twice; change the text and try again.
failure.tiktokUnaudited: TikTok has not audited this app yet, so it posts only to a private TikTok account. Until the audit passes, make the account private in TikTok (Settings and privacy → Privacy → Private account), then cancel this post and plan it again.
failure.tiktokPrivacy: the privacy chosen for this post is not offered for this TikTok account (an app TikTok has not audited may post as "Only me" only); cancel it and post it again with a privacy the posting screen offers.
failure.tiktokCap: the TikTok account reached its daily limit of posts, or of drafts waiting in its inbox, through apps; try again tomorrow, or post from the TikTok app.
failure.tiktokAppCap: the platform's TikTok app reached its daily limit of users posting through it (TikTok's cap for apps); try again tomorrow.
failure.tiktokBanned: TikTok does not let this account post at the moment; check the account in the TikTok app.
failure.tiktokDomain: TikTok pulls photos only from a domain verified for the app; verify the media domain in TikTok's developer portal (URL properties), or post a video.
failure.tiktokSpam: TikTok flagged the post as spam or risky and will not publish it; change the caption before posting again.
failure.tiktokMedia: TikTok refused the media (its format, length, frame rate or picture size); check it against TikTok's requirements and post it again.
